paraphrase: Some mathematical facts are causally relevant to physical outcomes, e.g. the primeness of 13 and 17 is part of what brings about periodical cicadas' life-cycle lengths. So something without esse in re (a number or mathematical fact) does causal work.
note: Analyst causal reading of Alan Baker's cicada case ('Are there genuine mathematical explanations of physical phenomena?', Mind 114, 2005), attribution deferred: no pinned witness. Baker argues for explanatory indispensability, and most discussants read the explanation as non-causal; only the causal reading is a rival to the weak version.
